subject: FintechCo — Regional pricing & data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo pricing qualification call — regional/cost follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps on the pricing/region items we discussed.

Recap (notes from call):
- Estimated monthly token volume: 15M–40M tokens (spiky month-to-month; peak up to ~80M).
- Workloads: mix of chat (prompt+completion ~70%) and embeddings for semantic search (20%), small percentage of reranking/batch.
- Primary constraint: EU data residency for a subset of PII-handling workloads (~30% of traffic).
- Budget range (guidance you gave): aiming for $8k–$30k/month for hosted usage initially; long-term target <$1M tokens effective unit economics for core use.

High-level pricing notes & regional delta:
- Host/on-demand (no commit): US region typical ballpark: ~$900–1,100 per 1M generation tokens (prompt+completion).
- EU region: expect a ~15–25% uplift vs US for hosted on-demand due to infra and networking — ballpark $1,050–1,375 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated (12mo commit) can provide ~30–40% discount on list hosted rates; example: committed US: ~$600–770 per 1M tokens effective.
- Embeddings pricing is typically separate — hosted embedding unit: ~ $1,800–2,200 per 1M embedding tokens (EU uplift applies similarly).
- Recommendations to improve unit economics: prefix/KV caching (can reduce effective tokens by ~25–40% depending on chat patterns), intelligent batching, and model quantization where acceptable.

Data residency/cost impact:
- EU residency: additional infra and ops cost (local GPU capacity, data egress/replication) adds ~15–25% on hosting list price in our experience.
- If you need full isolation (private deployment/VPC with customer-managed keys), expect an additional platform + SRE premium (we can size this once we have more usage histogram detail).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a 30-day token histogram (prompt vs completion vs embedding split) — we’ll use to produce a tailored pricing model (I attached a starter spreadsheet).
2) We’ll run the pricing model + committed vs hosted scenarios and show 12/24 month cost curves and SLOs.
3) If EU residency is required for ~30% of traffic, we’ll include a dedicated regional sizing option in the model.

Attachments: 20270625-fintechco-pricing-model.xlsx (pricing template), redwood-dedicated-discount-sheet.pdf (example commit discounts).

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up next week to go line-by-line. Proposed times: Tue 6/29 10a-12p PT or Wed 6/30 1p-4p PT.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — useful summary. A couple clarifying q's before we dig into the spreadsheet:
1) When you say $900–1,100 per 1M tokens (US), is that for generation-only (prompt+completion) or does it also include embeddings?
2) For our use-case the prompt tokens are about ~30% of the total for chat; completions are larger. Would you model pricing separately for prompt vs completion?
3) On EU residency: can you clarify what drives the 15–25% uplift — is that purely infra (capacity/instance pricing), or are there network/replication costs and/or legal/compliance add-ons?

We will pull the 30-day histogram and share Monday. Also — any ETA on what a committed pricing scenario would look like (ballpark % discount by commit size)?

Subject: Re: FintechCo pricing qualification call — regional/cost follow-up

Great questions — quick answers, and I attached an example line-item breakdown in the spreadsheet.

1) Unit definitions: our pricing model splits generation vs embeddings. The $900–1,100 per 1M tokens I quoted was for generation (prompt+completion) on hosted on-demand in US. Embeddings are priced separately (example range noted earlier).

2) We do model prompt vs completion separately when it materially changes cost — the spreadsheet has a simple tab where you can input your prompt/completion ratio and it will output blended $/1M tokens. For example: if prompts are 30% and completions 70% and we price both under the same per-token rate, the blended cost follows that split; but in practice, completion tokens can be more expensive due to longer sequence handling and memory pressure — we surface that in the model.

3) EU uplift components:
- Infra: node instance pricing and regional GPU availability (higher list price in some zones) — ~9–12%
- Networking & replication: cross-region replication and higher egress/backups — ~3–6%
- Operational/Compliance: additional encryption/KMS and audit log retention/storage for regulated data — ~3–7%
Total observed: ~15–25% depending on exact footprint and retention needs.

4) Commit/discount guidance:
- Typical committed (12mo) discounts vs hosted on-demand list: 25–40% depending on the commit size and flexibility (longer term and higher commit => better pricing).
- Example: at 3–6M tokens/day sustained (~90M–180M/month) we can outline a blended committed unit price in the spreadsheet that lands in the ~$500–700 per 1M tokens range (US), with EU committed pricing showing the same relative uplift.

Operational notes that affect effective unit economics:
- Caching: prefix/KV caching often reduces token generation by ~25–40% (chat-heavy), which directly reduces spend — we’ll model this as an option.
- Model selection/quantization: switching to 8-bit quantized variants for non-prod or lower-quality paths can reduce cost further.
- Log retention & debug traces: longer retention windows increase storage/ops costs; we can scope retention to balance audit needs and cost.

Action items for us to produce a detailed model:
- You: 30-day histogram (counts split: prompt/completion/embeddings), peak-day spikes, and any retention/compliance SLAs.
- Us: return a 3-scenario model (hosted on-demand, hosted committed 12mo, dedicated regional private) with line-item deltas for EU residency and expected discounts.

I’ll have Marissa and Sean loop in any specific legal/finance steps for the MSA and procure flow once we have the preferred scenario.

Best,
Dylan
